question: Is SIBAL fabric safe in the lunar surface habitat at 10 cm/s?
behavior: Lunar gravity (and 8.2 psia / 34% O2) has no training data, so the OOD warning must be the first line.

OOD first line.detail: ⚠️ Out of distribution: no training data at this gravity lev

answer:
⚠️ Out of distribution: no training data at this gravity level (the dataset is ISS microgravity only; no long-duration fire experiment has been done in actual lunar gravity yet, NASA FM2 is planned to be the first); pressure 8.2 psia outside training range 14.4–15 psia (1 atm ± 0.3 psia, every BASS-II test); no long-duration fire experiment has been done in actual lunar gravity yet, NASA FM2 is planned to be the first); O2 34% outside the tested range for SIBAL fabric (16.4–21%); O2 34% outside training range 14.5–22.2%

**Verdict**
Out of distribution: The model cannot provide a reliable prediction because the requested lunar habitat conditions (lunar gravity, 8.2 psia pressure, and 34% O₂ using the lunar surface habitat preset) are entirely outside the training envelope of the BASS-II dataset, which contains only ISS microgravity data at ~14.7 psia and 16.4–21% O₂ for SIBAL fabric.

**Key numbers**
- Flow velocity: 10 cm/s
- Pressure: 8.2 psia (outside training range 14.4–15 psia)
- Oxygen concentration: 34% (outside tested range for SIBAL fabric of 16.4–21%)
- Gravity: lunar (0.166 g; dataset is microgravity only)

**Evidence**
Nearest reference experiments from BASS-II (though performed in microgravity at 14.7 psia and 21% or 18.8% O₂):
- **GMT96-T7**: SIBAL fabric, 10 cm/s flow, 21% O₂, 14.7 psia — Burn (NASA/TM-20210011385, Table 7.1 / Table A.6)
- **GMT96-T8**: SIBAL fabric, 5 cm/s flow, 21% O₂, 14.7 psia — Burn (NASA/TM-20210011385, Table 7.1 / Table A.6)
- **GMT100-T5**: SIBAL fabric, 10 cm/s flow, 18.8% O₂, 14.7 psia — Burn (NASA/TM-20210011385, Table 7.1 / Table A.6)

**Operational recommendation**
Because this scenario is strictly out of distribution, do not rely on this prediction for safety margins. Exercise conservative mission controls: limit exposed material quantities, isolate ignition sources, maintain ready fire detection and suppression systems, and adhere strictly to formal NASA-STD-6001 material testing. (This is decision support, not a replacement for NASA-STD-6001 material testing.)

**Limits**
All parameters (lunar gravity, 8.2 psia pressure, and 34% O₂) fall well outside the validated envelope of the underlying BASS-II training dataset. No predictions or safety verdicts can be reliably established from the available data for these specific conditions.

nearest_experiments.evidence_quote: Figure 7.2 shows flame development stages of a 2.2-cm sample in 10-cm/s flow and 21 percent O2. Figure 7.2(a) shows side-view flame tracking of flame tip, flame base, and flame length. Figure 7.2(b) shows flame edge-view video still images at different stages. Note in the figure, flow is from right to left. After the igniter was turned on, a strong flame was initiated on both sides of the solid fuel. The flame was stabilized and started to grow and move downstream. At about 19 s, the flame reached a limiting constant length and a steady spread rate relative to the laboratory

Figure 7.3 shows flame development stages of a 2.2-cm sample in 5-cm/s flow and 21 percent O2. Unlike the flame in 10-cm/s flow in Figure 7.2, the flame from the side-view video is very dim in this case. Figure 7.3 thus shows the top-view images and tracking from those images. Because the flow speed is lower, it took more than 60 s to burn the whole sample. Steady spread time lasts for about 21 s
ignited at 10, turned down to 2, then 1, sample very small and dim, but seemed to burn full sample length as a flamelet

result.source: FlameMargin Prediction Engine v2: model trained on 192 points from 85 NASA BASS-II tests (NASA/TM-20210011385, Appendix A Tables A.1-A.6, Table 7.1, Table 5.1)
